programme.title: Would I Lie to You
programme.desc: Rob Brydon hosts a festive edition of the comedy panel show. Regular team captains David Mitchell and Lee Mack are joined by Jools Holland, Swarzy Shire, Helen George and David Walliams as they try to hoodwink their opponents with absurd facts and plausible lies about themselves.

programme.title: Tabby McTat
programme.desc: Animated adaptation of the Julia Donaldson book. Tabby McTat the singing cat and his busker friend Fred entertain the crowds of London, but become separated when Fred breaks his leg while pursuing a thief. Lost and alone, Tabby is taken in by a friendly fellow cat and finds a whole new life for herself with a kindly family - leaving him torn between two very different homes. Narrated by Jodie Whittaker, with the voices of Rob Brydon and Sopé Dirísu.

programme.title: The Croods 2: A New Age
programme.desc: Still searching for a place to settle down, prehistoric patriarch Grug leads his family to the great unknown. Hoping for the best in an increasingly dangerous world, while trying to come to terms with Eep and Guy's budding romance, Grug stumbles upon a secluded Eden of plenty, containing everything that they have been seeking. However, there is a catch. This area is already occupied by the significantly more evolved Bettermans - Phil, Hope and their daughter Dawn. Animated comedy sequel, with the voices of Nicolas Cage, Emma Stone and Ryan Reynolds.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin Roberts is joined by celebrated interior designer Laurence Llewelyn-Bowen to look around a three-bedroom terrace just outside Bristol. Needless to say, Laurence falls in love with its avocado bathroom suite. There's also a trawl through the show's archives of 2005, when Martin saw a disused former public toilet that was up for sale at auction. Jacqui Joseph is in Essex to see a three bed semi that's crumbling from the outside and letting the street down.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp introduces a special edition celebrating antiques and collectables from around the world. From fabulous French glass and sparking Scandinavian jewellery to amazing antiques from Asia and Africa, this episode delves into the archive to remember some of the most memorable buys from around the globe. At the National Museum of Scotland in Edinburgh, Natasha gets a tour of a gallery bursting with European furniture, including a few trend-setting examples which wouldn't look out of place in the modern home.

programme.title: Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile
programme.desc: Joseph and Katie Primm and their young son Josh move into a New York City house, where Lyle, a singing crocodile, has been left to fend for himself by a charismatic magician. Musical comedy based on the book series by Bernard Waber, with songs by The Greatest Showman's Benj Pasek and Justin Paul. Starring Javier Bardem, Constance Wu and Winslow Fegley.

programme.title: Back to the Future Part II
programme.desc: Time-travelling teenager Marty McFly travels to the 21st century, where he has to save his children from a terrible fate. However, this proves to have unforeseen consequences when the future version of arch enemy Biff sees a chance to rewrite history for his own benefit, leaving Marty stuck in a twisted parallel universe. Sci-fi comedy sequel, starring Michael J Fox and Christopher Lloyd.

programme.title: Celebrity Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents a pop star special of the high-stakes quiz, with Sinitta, Ian 'H' Watkins from Steps, Ritchie Neville from Five and Una Healy from The Saturdays playing to win money for their chosen charities. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong and Richard Osman present as Mark Stacey, Catherine Southon, Kye Whyte, Dan Powell, Anjli Mohindra, Meera Syal, Rosie Jones and Suzi Ruffell try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Singer, musician and actor Chesney Hawkes looks for a rural hideaway, to escape the bright lights and big stages. Jules Hudson has a selection of chart-topping character homes and is optimistic that the Cotswolds countryside will be a smash-hit for rockstar Chesney and his wife Krissy, along with their three grown-up children. On the billing are exquisite interiors, cottage charm and property perfection, but can Jules persuade Chesney to swap leather for tweed at the manorial Mystery House?.(New).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: A situation escalates at Jimmy's christening, Kojo attempts to help a friend, and the drama of Christmas is far from over for one family.

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles and the team step in to help a youth club that has lost its home in the town of Beverley, East Yorkshire. The Cherry Tree Community Centre once gave local children a safe place to meet up and find support - but when the pandemic hit, the building was turned into a food hub for families, leaving the kids out in the cold. With another harsh winter on the way, Nick, designer Gabrielle Blackman and the DIY SOS regulars enlist the help of local tradespeople - as well as a few Gladiators - to construct a new, purpose-built youth centre on the edge of the park.(New).

programme.title: The Apprentice
programme.desc: Part two of two. After a festive trip to Lapland, the celebrities head back to London to pitch their Christmas biscuits to supermarket giants and retailers. Both teams rope in their famous friends to do their best to raise money in aid of Children in Need but in the boardroom, it's all business and one of the celebrities faces the firing finger.(New).

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of the latest Premier League matches, including Arsenal v Aston Villa at Emirates Stadium and Manchester United v Wolverhampton Wanderers at Old Trafford. Arsenal will be hoping to be crowned champions for the first time since 2004 this term, but had failed to win at home to the Villans in each of the last two seasons. The Red Devils lost home and away to Wolves in 2024/25, but the Midlanders have struggled in the current campaign. Plus, Burnley v Newcastle United, Chelsea v Bournemouth, Nottingham Forest v Everton and West Ham United v Brighton & Hove Albion.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: When Eric and Beth put their tree up earlier than usual, they unwittingly kick off the Christmas season in Latimer Crescent. What starts as a labour-saving convenience quickly turns into a flurry of festive activity as their son Ian and partner Gordon, neighbours Colin, Cathy, Christine, Michelle and Alan start to gear up for the holidays in their own unique ways. Festive edition of the comedy, starring Arabella Weir, Alex Norton, Elaine C Smith, Doon Mackichan and Jonathan Watson.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: The doting matriarch rediscovers the meaning of family as she gathers those closest to her together for a Christmas photo. Buster unveils another of his signature Christmas trees with maximum impact and Cathy frets about what presents to buy everyone. First of two festive specials, starring Brendan O'Carroll, Jennifer Gibney and Danny O'Carroll.

programme.title: Superworm
programme.desc: Animated adaptation of Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler's children's book. Garden-dwelling hero Superworm is always on hand to help the other animals - but his best friend Butterfly never gets any of the credit for helping him save the day. When Superworm is kidnapped by a greedy lizard wizard on the hunt for treasure, Butterfly comes up with a daring plan to rescue him. Narrated by Olivia Colman, with the voices of Matt Smith, Patricia Allison, and Rob Brydon.

programme.title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
programme.desc: One-inch-tall, googly-eyed talking shell Marcel lives with his grandmother Nana Connie, who is in the early stages of dementia. Filmmaker Dean rents the house and becomes fascinated by the day-to-day activities of his tiny housemate. Animated comedy, directed by and starring Dean Fleischer Camp, with Thomas Mann, Rosa Salazar, and the voices of Jenny Slate and Isabella Rossellini.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.sub-title: Celebrity Special with Dion and Steel from Gladiators
programme.desc: Steel from Gladiators joins Dion Dublin to renovate an end-of-terrace property in Newcastle-under-Lyme and Martin Roberts is left in awe of a granite-built property in Cornwall. In a clip from the archive, Dion gets a makeover during a visit to a Rochdale barber shop.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles hosts as experts Raj Bisram and Stephanie Connell, help two teams bargain-hunting in Norwich. While Eric is in the city, he visits the museum at Norwich Castle to discover more about the ancient mammals that once populated East Anglia.

programme.title: The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse
programme.desc: Animated adaptation of Charlie Mackesy's popular illustrated book about a boy and his animal companions, who share a series of brief but profound conversations on the nature of friendship as they journey together in the youngster's search for home. With the voices of Tom Hollander, Idris Elba, Gabriel Byrne and newcomer Jude Coward Nicoll.

programme.title: Back to the Future Part III
programme.desc: Time-travelling teenager Marty McFly is transported back to the days of the Wild West, where he strives to save his eccentric scientist friend Doc Brown from death at the hands of a villainous gunslinger. Final instalment in the sci-fi comedy trilogy, starring Michael J Fox, Christopher Lloyd, Mary Steenburgen and Thomas F Wilson.

programme.title: Despicable Me 3
programme.desc: Dismissed from the Anti-Villain League after botching a mission, Gru sets off to meet his long-lost twin brother for one final criminal mission. Animated sequel, with the voices of Steve Carell, Kristen Wiig, Trey Parker and Miranda Cosgrove.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong and Richard Osman present a comedians' edition of the general knowledge quiz. Rosie Holt, Nabil Abdulrashid, Shaparak Khorsandi, Mark Steel, Lou Sanders, Luke McQueen, Amy Gledhill and Chris Cantrill try to come up with the least likely correct answers to a series of questions posed to members of the public to win money for the charity of their choice.

programme.title: The Weakest Link
programme.desc: Romesh Ranganathan is joined by Charlotte Crosby, Patsy Palmer, Keith Brymer Jones, Ian 'H' Watkins, Fatiha El-Ghorri, Merlin Griffiths, Bash the Entertainer and Luke Hamnett for another festive edition. As always, the celebrities will initially have to work together to try to win up to £50,000 for their individual chosen charity, with one player voted off by their fellow contestants at the end of each round.(New).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: New Year Celebrations take over Walford, the Brannings turn on one of their own, and Phil offers advice.

programme.title: Here We Go
programme.desc: With the new year fast approaching, Rachel is keen to throw a massive party, although Paul would much rather the family welcomed in 2026 in a quiet holiday cottage - preferably one with a sauna so he can sweat out the massive boil on his cheek. Cue a typically chaotic Jessop holiday, involving a road trip, a missing dummy and a large crate of unlicensed fireworks picked up at a police auction. Festive special of the comedy, starring Katherine Parkinson and Jim Howick, with Alison Steadman, Tom Basden and Freya Parks.(New).

programme.title: Mission: Impossible
programme.desc: Secret agents suspect there is a traitor in their organisation when their latest assignment ends in disaster. The sole survivor is accused of being the mole, forcing him to go on the run to clear his name. However, in the process, he discovers a former Russian spy is selling information about the world's leading undercover operatives. Action thriller based on the 1960s TV series, starring Tom Cruise, Jon Voight and Ving Rhames.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: A round-up of today's headlines.

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show
programme.desc: The host rings in the new year in the company of Tom Hiddleston, who is set to return as spy Jonathan Pine in the second series of The Night Manager. Also appearing are Oscar-winner Laura Dern and comic actor Will Arnett, who are starring together in Is This Thing On?, inspired by the life of comedian John Bishop. Owen Cooper, the young star of TV phenomenon Adolescence, also joins the host, while triple Oscar-nominee Carey Mulligan and comedian Tim Key discuss their part in feelgood British hit The Ballad of Wallis Island. Plus, Alison Limerick performs her classic dance hit Where Love Lives.(New).

programme.title: Ronan Keating and Friends: New Year's Eve Party
programme.desc: The former Boyzone frontman becomes the latest singer to present a New Year's Eve concert, performing hits including the two-time platinum-selling When You Say Nothing at All, the track that catapulted him to international status when the song was chosen for box office smash Notting Hill. He also performs his number one single Life Is a Rollercoaster, which has clocked up over a 100 million streams, along with many more tracks from across his career and timeless songs from artists including George Michael and Van Morrison. Ronan is joined by his touring band, as well as some very special guests.(New).

programme.title: New Year's Eve Fireworks
programme.desc: The people of London gather on the Thames Embankment to bid goodbye to 2025 and welcome in a new year. The traditional chimes of Big Ben herald the dawn of 2026, followed by a spectacular fireworks display that will light up the sky over the river, before the singing of Auld Lang Syne.(New).

programme.title: Ronan Keating and Friends: New Year's Eve Party
programme.desc: The music picks up again as Ronan and his guests continue rocking into 2026.(New).

programme.title: Glastonbury 2025
programme.desc: Clara Amfo and Lauren Laverne present Rod Stewart's Pyramid Stage performance from June, his first appearance at the festival in over 20 years, having previously headlined in 2002. Songs include The First Cut Is the Deepest, You Wear It Well, Maggie May, I'd Rather Go Blind, Do Ya Think I'm Sexy?, I Don't Want to Talk About It and Stay with Me.

programme.title: Tiddler
programme.desc: Animated adaptation of Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler's children's book about a little fish with a big imagination, who gets lost in the deep wide ocean. But his gift for storytelling may be just what he needs to find his way safely home. Narrated by Hannah Waddingham, and featuring the voices of Lolly Adefope, Jayde Adams and Rob Brydon.

programme.title: Abominable
programme.desc: After discovering a magical creature they believe to be a Yeti, teenager Yi and her two friends embark on an epic adventure. They try to reunite the creature with his family, whilst evading a wealthy financier and a determined zoologist who want to capture the creature for their own needs. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Chloe Bennet, Albert Tsai and Tenzing Norgay Trainor.

programme.title: Minions: The Rise of Gru
programme.desc: Young Gru attends an interview to join a diabolical dream team christened the Vicious 6, but Belle Bottom, Jean-Clawed, Nun-chuck, Svengeance and Stronghold cruelly dismiss the boy. In retaliation for the ageist snub, the resourceful tyke steals an ancient amulet that can harness the power of the 12 creatures of the Chinese zodiac. Animated comedy prequel, featuring the voices of Steve Carell, Alan Arkin, Taraji P Henson and Jean-Claude Van Damme.

programme.title: Gladiators
programme.desc: Bradley and Barney Walsh present a special edition of the contest, in which four famous faces take on tests of speed, strength and skill. The nation's favourite PE teacher Joe Wicks competes against TV and radio presenter Sam Thompson, while boxing favourite Nicola Adams takes on podcaster Vogue Williams.

programme.title: The Archbishop of Canterbury Elect's New Year Message
programme.desc: Prior to her confirmation in the role later in the month, the Rt Rev Sarah Mullally delivers a message of hope, reconciliation and reflection.(New).

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: Adaptation of the children's book by Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler, starring Rob Brydon, Jessie Buckley and Domhnall Gleeson. Two devoted scarecrows, Betty O'Barley and Harry O'Hay, plan a wedding to remember but, when Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon Betty's in danger and everything is at risk - can Harry get back in time and save the day?

programme.title: BBC Proms 2025
programme.desc: Claudia Winkleman hosts this musical exploration of her phenomenon ratings success. From epic classical orchestral favourites to opera excerpts with betrayal at their heart, this Prom, recorded in July at the Royal Albert Hall, features melodramatic chart tracks heard on the series with a gothic, symphonic twist. There's a new take on the theme tune and some familiar figures and faces from the challenges and round tables. Conjuring the misty intrigue are soloists Andrea Lykke, HAYLA and Darrell Smith, alongside the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra under conductor Karen Ní Bhroin and BBC Singers in works by composers including Rob Dougan, Sam Watts, Saint-Saëns, Mozart, Tchaikovsky and Puccini.(New).

programme.title: The Sound of Music
programme.desc: A cheerful novice nun is employed as governess to the seven children of an austere widower. As she brings light, laughter and a love of all things harmonious to a family previously beset by grief and strict discipline she also falls in love with her employer. But before long, the looming threat of the Second World War jeopardises their happy household. Oscar-winning Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, starring Julie Andrews, Christopher Plummer and Eleanor Parker.

programme.title: Wild London
programme.desc: Having lived in London for 75 years, David Attenborough shares his intimate knowledge of the city's natural history. London is considered the greenest city in the world with a surprising variety of animal dramas playing out in the most unexpected places - whether it's pigeons commuting by the Tube, snakes slithering along Regent's canal, parakeets raiding city parks or beavers building a home next to a busy shopping centre. The veteran naturalist celebrates the extraordinary ways animals adapt to survive in the urban jungle and the inspiring initiatives to encourage nature back into the city.(New).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: One year on from the present day, Max Branning finds himself in a situation which will have huge consequences for not only himself, but also his family. With multiple situations unfolding at once on January 1, 2027, it becomes clear that 2026 has many secrets waiting to be discovered, and a heap of trouble that would be hard for any one person to talk themselves out of.

programme.title: The Traitors
programme.desc: Twenty-two people from across the UK descend on a Scottish castle in a bid to win up to £120,000, some to be assigned by host Claudia Winkleman as traitors, while the majority are faithful. Suspicions, secrets and lies echo around the castle, as under the cover of darkness, the Traitors must pick off the residual players one by one, eliminating them from the game. The faithful must try to work out who the traitors are in their midst, banishing them from the game before becoming their next victim. Those who make it to the final have a chance of winning the life-changing cash prize.(New).

programme.title: The Night Manager
programme.desc: Tom Hiddleston reprises his role as soldier-turned-hotel night manager Jonathan Pine in the long-awaited return of the acclaimed drama. The story picks up after nine years with Jonathan living as Alex Goodwin, a low-level MI6 officer running a quiet surveillance unit in London. His life is comfortingly uneventful until the chance sighting of former mercenary connected with arms dealer Richard Roper prompts a call to action and leads him to a violent encounter with a new player - Colombian businessman Teddy Dos Santos. Once in Colombia, Pine is plunged deep into a deadly plot to destabilise the country. With Olivia Colman, Diego Calva and Douglas Hodge.(New).

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Tensions are high as Agnes and the gang prepare for an incoming storm. Buster's flying high as he nervously awaits his birthday parachute jump, Winnie receives a shock to the system, and a lost nun is in need of help. Seasonal comedy capers, starring Brendan O'Carroll.(New).

programme.title: Shedites
programme.desc: One-off comedy set in and around the sheds in an Irish village, where the men make themselves useful building and repairing things, and along the way find company through unlikely friendships, a sense of purpose and a strong cup of tea. Here they set out to build a new bike from spare parts to win a local race, leading to plenty of shenanigans, bruised pride and a fair dose of stubbornness. Starring Phil Davis, Brendan O'Carroll, Simon Delaney, Paddy Houlihan and Deirdre O'Kane.(New).

programme.title: Mission: Impossible 2
programme.desc: Secret agent Ethan Hunt is sent to find and destroy the only sample of a deadly man-made virus. However, he faces tough opposition in a former spy-turned-criminal mastermind who has already acquired the cure and now wants the pathogen itself. Director John Woo's action thriller sequel, starring Tom Cruise, Dougray Scott, Thandiwe Newton and Anthony Hopkins.

programme.title: The Apprentice
programme.desc: Part one of two. AJ Odudu, Angela Scanlon, Charlie Hedges, Eddie Kadi, Jake Wood, JB Gill, Kadeena Cox, Matt Morsia, Rob Rinder, Sarah Hadland, Shazia Mirza and Tom Skinner compete to raise money for Children in Need. Lord Sugar splits the celebrities into two teams, under the watchful eyes of Karren Brady and Mike Soutar, and sends them to Lapland to create their own twist on the classic gingerbread biscuit before producing an advert and jingle, and pitching to retailers. For the first time in Celebrity Apprentice history, the products will be on sale to the public to raise money for Children in Need.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Judi Dench joins Charlotte Smith in the grounds of Inveraray Castle to reflect on the impact the countryside has had on her and her family. She's also joined by her grandson Sam to check in on a tartan that's being created for her in which every thread tells a personal story. Adam Henson meets her partner David Mills, who gave up dairying to create the British Wildlife Centre on his Surrey farm, while wildlife film-maker Hamza Yassin helps her fulfil a lifetime ambition to see golden eagles in the wild.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The story of Anne the Asian elephant, who was rescued from the circus in poor health and is now one of the park's oldest and fittest animals. Hamza Yassin plays spot the difference with a pair of wildebeest.

programme.sub-title: Celebrity Special with Owain and Ian `H" Watkins
programme.desc: Owain Wyn Evans shows Ian 'H' Watkins from Steps around a tiny home in the historic town of Stratford-upon-Avon and Martel Maxwell visits a damp mid-terrace property in Preston. In a clip from the archives, Martin Roberts visits a barnstorming farmhouse in Lincolnshire.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents from Shepton Mallet, Somerset, with the reds and the blue teams being guided by experts John Cameron and Stephanie Connell. During the contest, Natasha learns about the history of wristwatches, and checks out a seriously valuable collection.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Bill Paterson reminisces about four favourite sporting fixes. The items are a rugby league cap given to a Yorkshireman who played for his country, a wooden skateboard bought in 1967, a horse saddle from the 1920s and a speedway bib that used to belong to a racer from the Bristol Bulldogs in 1947.

programme.title: I Escaped to the Country
programme.desc: Denise Nurse enjoys a tour of TV medic Dr Ranj Singh's freshly decorated, sky-high water tower. Once the 'mystery' house, it's now Ranj's personal fitness regime, thanks largely to its five flights of stairs. Denise huffs and puffs her way to the top to find the doctor hosting his housewarming party.(New).

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Charlie Dimmock head to Manchester to transform Mona and Qurban's awkward L-shaped, building-site garden into a Moroccan courtyard. The pair want a garden that has the atmosphere of country, geometric and with warm colours, Majorelle blue pots and Islamic motifs, so they can enjoy a space that echoes their travels and which they can share with their children..(New).

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Comedy actor, panto dame and former King of the Jungle Christopher Biggins and his partner Neil escape London for a new home in the rural Home Counties. The trio take a trip to Highclere Castle, aka Downton Abbey, where Biggins wonders how to go about getting a part in one of the most popular shows of all time. Presented by Nicki Chapman.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You
programme.desc: Comedians Chris McCausland and Harriet Kemsley, actress Julie Hesmondhalgh and broadcaster Yinka Bokinni join host Rob Brydon and regular captains David Mitchell and Lee Mack on the offbeat panel show. As usual, the participants set out to hoodwink their opponents with absurd facts and plausible fibs about themselves in a bid to secure a team victory, through rounds such as Home Truths and Quick-fire Lies.(New).

programme.title: The Traitors
programme.desc: As the players face a new day, all faithfuls wonder who has survived the night and will make it to breakfast. It isn't long before they attempt to increase the prize-pot in the mission, but whose focus is on the money and who is focused on safety from murder? The game suddenly becomes very real as the first dramatic banishment takes place, proving that at the round table there is nowhere to hide. Leaving the players little time to gather their thoughts, the traitors eye up their next victim. Hosted by Claudia Winkleman.(New).

programme.title: The Traitors: Uncloaked
programme.desc: Ed Gamble discusses all the latest treachery from the castle with Joe Marler and Tom and Alex from series one, plus any murdered or banished players from the preceding episode.(New).

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Greek Job
programme.desc: Amanda Holden and Alan Carr renovate a derelict property on the Greek island of Corfu, intending the finished home to be sold with the proceeds going to charity. With ivy growing through the windows, hay and mud as a floor, a sewage pipe running through the downstairs plus a roof on the verge of caving in, their new project resembles a stable more than a house. While working on the project, the duo embrace the indigenous culture, make new friends and throw themselves into local life.(New).

programme.title: Mission: Impossible III
programme.desc: Former secret agent Ethan Hunt is called out of retirement when an ex-trainee is taken hostage by a ruthless arms dealer, but when the rescue operation goes wrong, the villain decides to target Hunt's fiancee. Action thriller sequel directed by JJ Abrams, starring Tom Cruise, Philip Seymour Hoffman, Michelle Monaghan, Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg.

Before dying he whispers a secret that has serious political implications - but they are prevented from telling the police when their son is kidnapped by a gang of spies bent on keeping them silent. Alfred Hitchcock's remake of his own 1934 thriller, with James Stewart, Doris Day, Bernard Miles and Daniel Gelin.

programme.desc: American writer Holly Martins goes to post-Second World War Vienna at the invitation of his old friend Harry Lime, only to be told that Lime has been killed by a car while crossing the street. However, the author finds the circumstances surrounding his death fail to add up and goes in search of the truth - but is unprepared for the ugly secrets he uncovers. Carol Reed's thriller, written by Graham Greene, starring Joseph Cotten, Orson Welles, Alida Valli and Trevor Howard.

Alfred Hitchcock's thriller, starring Ray Milland, Grace Kelly, Robert Cummings and John Williams.

He passes the time watching the comings and goings of his neighbours in the apartment block opposite and becomes convinced one of them has committed a murder. However, he has trouble persuading anyone to believe his story. Hitchcock thriller, starring James Stewart, Grace Kelly, Raymond Burr, Thelma Ritter and Judith Evelyn.

programme.desc: In 1975, wrestler Andy Robin and his wife Maggie adopted nine-month-old bear cub Hercules and, against all the odds, set out to tame one of the world's fiercest animals and what followed was an extraordinary tale of wrestling, rescue and super stardom. Featuring never seen before home video, this documentary revisits the incredible bond between Andy, Maggie and Hercules the bear.(New).

Without enough lifeboats to go around and no rescue mission in sight, everyone left faces a struggle for survival. As the situation gets more urgent, and in the face of a scramble to get in the remaining lifeboats, guns are handed out to the senior officers to maintain order.(New).

To help them decide the winner, judges Grace Dent and John Torode will be joined by restaurant critic Tom Parker Bowles.

The Red Devils lost home and away to Wolves in 2024/25, but the Midlanders have struggled in the current campaign. Her success, however, came at the price of a turbulent private life and an unhappy marriage to a gambler, who grew increasingly jealous of her fame. Starring an Oscar-winning Barbra Streisand, with Omar Sharif, Kay Medford and Walter Pidgeon.

programme.sub-title: Top of the Pops Review of the Year 2025
programme.desc: Clara Amfo looks back over the past 12 months in music, presenting performances by some of the biggest artists of 2025. Highlights include Mercury Prize winner Sam Fender and breakout star Lola Young at Radio 1's Big Weekend in Liverpool's Sefton Park. Plus, Lewis Capaldi's surprise slot at the Glastonbury Festival, chart record breaker Olivia Dean on Later? with Jools Holland, and some of the stories of the year from women taking over the headline slots at music festivals, with the likes of Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan topping the bill at Glastonbury and Reading Festival respectively. Jarvis Cocker reflects on his band Pulp making a return after 24 years, and US rising stars Ravyn Lenae and Alex Warren discuss having two of the biggest selling songs of the year.(New).

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Alex Brooker, Rhys Darby, Joanna Page and Molly Rainford test their general knowledge skills in a variety of trivia-based games for a special festive show.(New).

programme.title: Celebrity Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie asks the questions in another edition of the classic quiz where celebrities donate to their chosen charities. Drag performer Tia Kofi, actress Lauren Patel, comedian Josh Jones, and TV presenter and auctioneer Izzie Balmer answer questions on the Christopher Eccleston incarnation of Doctor Who, the Oscar-winning film musical La La Land, Lady Jane Grey, and guinea pigs.(New).

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Winners of the third-place play-offs from two different series compete against each other - the Poptimists and the Ramblers. Victoria Coren Mitchell presents.(New).

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.desc: It's the first semi-final of this special all-star seasonal series. Two of the highest-scoring winning teams from the heats return to play again. Amol Rajan asks the questions.(New).

programme.title: Titanic Sinks Tonight
programme.desc: The last wooden lifeboat leaves and the passengers and crew face their fates, with reactions ranging from the captain's shocked resignation, to designer Andrews' desperate bid to help others. Those in the lifeboats watch in horror as explosions boom, sparks fly and Titanic splits in two, with the lifeboat occupants facing a dilemma - to risk saving others or to prioritise their own survival.(New).

programme.title: The Full Monty
programme.desc: Six unemployed men from Sheffield decide to become strippers for one night only in a bid to raise extra money. However, with no dancing experience and far from perfect physiques, the men rely on the unique selling point of complete nudity to impress the punters. Comedy, starring Robert Carlyle, Mark Addy, Tom Wilkinson, Hugo Speer and Paul Barber.

programme.title: Jools' Annual Hootenanny
programme.desc: Jools Holland and his Rhythm & Blues Orchestra welcome in the new year with a stellar line-up of guests, including Rolling Stones guitarist Ronnie Wood, chart star Olivia Dean, veteran singer Lulu - performing her 1974 version of David Bowie's The Man Who Sold the World - and Jessie J, with her crowd-pleaser Living My Best Life. Also appearing are torch singer Imelda May, garage star Craig David, soul diva Heather Small, Brighton band the Kooks, boogie woogie queen Ruby Turner, Mercury Prize-nominated pianist Joe Webb and swing drummer David Hemlin.(New).

programme.title: 30 Hits of 1988 at the BBC
programme.desc: A journey through the BBC's music archives for a selection of songs from the year, including Kylie Minogue's I Should Be So Lucky as well as hits for Salt-N-Pepa, Terence Trent D'Arby and Glenn Medeiros. Plus, Milli Vanilli had the world at their feet in 1988, but ultimately ended up pop pariahs after the lip-synching scandal that exposed the fact that Girl You Know It's True was actually a big lie.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: New host Sophie Willan presents this festive special, inviting Strictly judge Anton Du Beke, comedian Lucy Beaumont, actress Susan Wokoma and Tom Wilson - better known to Gladiators fans as Hammer - to take part in a trio of sewing challenges. They must put their own twist on a pattern for a Santa present sack, turn second-hand party wear into outfits based on The Twelve Days of Christmas and create clothing for models inspired by their favourite seasonal treat. Judges Esme Young and Patrick Grant keep a close eye on every stitch and hem and decide which famous face deserves the festive title.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

programme.title: Wild Horses, the Rockies and Me
programme.desc: Wildlife cameraman Gordon Buchanan goes in search of wild horses in Canada's Rocky Mountains, finding a family group of two competing stallions, two mares and their two young foals. To understand more about the horses, and this unusual family dynamic in particular, Gordon immerses himself into their world, attempting to befriend them, earn their trust and experience their lives from within the herd, something that hasn't been attempted before.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway treks along the Pembrokeshire coastal path in search of beaches and bluebells, before heading from east to west in an attempt to find the best springtime trails in Wales.

programme.title: Letter from an Unknown Woman
programme.desc: A teenage girl becomes infatuated with a renowned concert pianist. As she grows older, her yearning for him develops into a deep and obsessive love. However, he only discovers the truth about her feelings when it is too late. Romantic drama directed by Max Ophuls, starring Joan Fontaine, Louis Jourdan, Marcel Journet, Mady Christians and Howard Freeman.

programme.title: New Year's Day Concert
programme.desc: The Vienna Philharmonic's traditional concert from the Golden Hall of the Musikverein in the heart of Vienna.(New).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross presents a special edition focused on furniture. From side tables to chests of drawers, he charts the evolving styles of furniture and takes a tour through the ages, from the Georgian era to the Art Deco years of the 1920s and '30s. Along the way, he uncovers items from the Bargain Hunt archive and counts down the most profitable pieces at auction. Plus, a host of Bargain Hunt experts join him to look back at items of furniture that competing teams have bought down the years.

programme.title: The Archbishop of Canterbury Elect's New Year Message
programme.desc: Prior to her confirmation in the role later in the month, the Rt Rev Sarah Mullally delivers a message of hope, reconciliation and reflection.(New).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Steve Brown helps a couple from Hertfordshire to find a new home in their favourite holiday destination of Cornwall, as well as meeting a local ceramicist.

programme.title: Lawrence of Arabia
programme.desc: An enigmatic British Army officer tries to unite the Arab nations against the Turks during the First World War, but comes into conflict with the military authorities when he engages the enemy with guerrilla tactics instead of more conventional methods. However, his increasingly torn loyalties leave him close to madness. Oscar-winning epic drama directed by David Lean, starring Peter O'Toole, Omar Sharif, Anthony Quinn, Alec Guinness and Jack Hawkins.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Social climber Hyacinth finds herself all at sea when she makes an unexpected discovery during a QE2 cruise that threatens to jeopardise her dream trip. Christmas special from 1993, starring Patricia Routledge, Clive Swift and Geoffrey Hughes.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Alex Brooker, Rhys Darby, Joanna Page and Molly Rainford put their general knowledge to the test in the penultimate round of challenges.(New).

programme.title: Celebrity Mastermind
programme.desc: Journalist and broadcaster Charlotte Hawkins, comedian Stephen Bailey, Amandaland star Ekow Quartey and chef and author Belles Berry are in the spotlight. Clive Myrie asks questions on André Rieu, singer Cheryl, Arsenal's Invincibles season and English physician Nicholas Culpeper, as well as the usual general knowledge round.(New).

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts as the Brews take on the Irregulars in an edition that celebrates singles, solos and everything that comes in groups of one. The questions are suitably singular, with one asking what connects Snap!, Absolute Garbage and The Immaculate Collection.

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.desc: Another two teams of notable alumni return to contest the second semi-final. Amol Rajan asks the questions.(New).

programme.title: The Traitors: Uncloaked
programme.desc: Ed Gamble presents the companion programme to the hit strategy show. He and his guests Lucy Beaumont, series three Traitor Minah, series two faithful Mollie and Traitors superfan Jack Remmington discuss the highlights of the opening episode, who stood out among the players and whether they think the chosen traitors will live up to the task.(New).

programme.title: Outnumbered
programme.desc: The first episode of the partly improvised sitcom looking at the trials of raising three young children. The siblings cause chaos when Sue loses her car keys just before the school run. Hugh Dennis and Claire Skinner star as the harassed parents.

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: A selection of the best moments from the V series, hosted by Sandi Toksvig, with Alan Davies and the panellists coming up with interesting answers.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of the latest Premier League matches, including Sunderland v Manchester City at Stadium of Light and Liverpool v Leeds United at Anfield. Title-challenging City faced a potentially difficult assignment away to a Sunderland side who had impressed this term after winning the Championship play-offs, while the Reds faced another promoted side who had found things more difficult at times in their return to the top flight. Plus, Crystal Palace v Fulham and Brentford v Tottenham Hotspur.

programme.title: Titanic Sinks Tonight
programme.desc: From the crucial seconds before the collision to the final moments when the hull sank beneath the waves, this dramatised documentary pieces together events minute by minute to reveal what happened to the 2,208 passengers and crew of RMS Titanic on the night of April 14. 1912. This opening instalment begins with lookout crew member Fred Fleet spotting a black mass right ahead of Titanic and alerting the navigation crew, but the ship still hits the iceberg and news of the damage filters through to the captain.

programme.title: Titanic Sinks Tonight
programme.desc: The captain orders the ship to be evacuated and tells the wireless operators to send out an urgent distress call to other ships, while down below in the boiler rooms, the crew pump out the incoming sea water to buy the ship more time. With only enough lifeboats for half the people on board, a rescue mission requires shuttle runs to be made to and from a rescue ship. First-class passengers are handed life-preservers and told to make their way to the boat deck, but they have not been told the ship is sinking.

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: Paddy McGuinness and Cherry Healey visit the Original Biscuit Bakers factory in Market Drayton, Shropshire, to learn how they produce 100,000 gingerbread biscuits each week. Historian Ruth Goodman joins astronaut Helen Sharman to explore Christmas in space and Bobby Seagull teaches Cherry how to wrap presents using maths.

programme.title: Here We Go
programme.desc: With the new year fast approaching, Rachel is keen to throw a massive party, although Paul would much rather the family welcomed in 2026 in a quiet holiday cottage - preferably one with a sauna so he can sweat out the massive boil on his cheek. Cue a typically chaotic Jessop holiday, involving a road trip, a missing dummy and a large crate of unlicensed fireworks picked up at a police auction. Festive special of the comedy, starring Katherine Parkinson and Jim Howick, with Alison Steadman, Tom Basden and Freya Parks.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Children's TV presenter, child rights advocate and peer Floella Benjamin reveals what makes Christmas special for her, in this in-depth conversation, explaining how the season has been a marker for memorable moments in her career, family life and faith.

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Alex Brooker, Rhys Darby, Joanna Page and Molly Rainford put their general knowledge to the test in the penultimate round of challenges.

programme.title: Wild London
programme.desc: Having lived in London for 75 years, David Attenborough shares his intimate knowledge of the city's natural history. London is considered the greenest city in the world with a surprising variety of animal dramas playing out in the most unexpected places - whether it's pigeons commuting by the Tube, snakes slithering along Regent's canal, parakeets raiding city parks or beavers building a home next to a busy shopping centre. The veteran naturalist celebrates the extraordinary ways animals adapt to survive in the urban jungle and the inspiring initiatives to encourage nature back into the city.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of the latest Premier League matches, including Sunderland v Manchester City at Stadium of Light and Liverpool v Leeds United at Anfield. Title-challenging City faced a potentially difficult assignment away to a Sunderland side who had impressed this term after winning the Championship play-offs, while the Reds faced another promoted side who had found things more difficult at times in their return to the top flight. Plus, Crystal Palace v Fulham and Brentford v Tottenham Hotspur.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway rambles by one of Britain's best beaches and a legendary Welsh chapel, before heading on a tour of the Elan Valley that takes him past drowned villages to the famous Dambuster team's secret training ground.(New).

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Interviews with British comedy stars of the silver screen, featuring the likes of George Formby, Peter Sellers and the Monty Python team. Narrated by Sylvia Syms.

programme.title: Passport to Pimlico
programme.desc: The residents of a London suburb discover documents proving their neighbourhood is not part of Britain, and declare independence. Appointing their own head of state, they begin erecting borders as the government resorts to desperate measures to bring the community back under British rule. Ealing comedy, starring Stanley Holloway and Margaret Rutherford.

programme.title: A Man for All Seasons
programme.desc: Henry VIII's decision to divorce Catherine of Aragon leads to a clash with the Roman Catholic Church and his own lord chancellor Sir Thomas More. To force his will, the king declares himself the supreme head of the Church of England and demands More's approval - but when he fails to get it, he puts his former adviser on trial for his life. Oscar-winning adaptation of Robert Bolt's history play, with Paul Scofield, Robert Shaw, Wendy Hiller, Leo McKern, John Hurt and Orson Welles.

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles and the team step in to help a youth club that has lost its home in the town of Beverley, East Yorkshire. The Cherry Tree Community Centre once gave local children a safe place to meet up and find support - but when the pandemic hit, the building was turned into a food hub for families, leaving the kids out in the cold. With another harsh winter on the way, Nick, designer Gabrielle Blackman and the DIY SOS regulars enlist the help of local tradespeople - as well as a few Gladiators - to construct a new, purpose-built youth centre on the edge of the park.

programme.title: Ben-Hur
programme.desc: A Jewish prince in first-century Jerusalem is reunited with an old Roman friend, who is now the governor of Judea. However, their differing political views over local dissent leads to a bitter quarrel, and the governor uses the pretext of an accident to sell him into slavery and imprison his mother and sister. Years later, the prince returns, determined to seek revenge and find his missing family. Oscar-winning epic, starring Charlton Heston, Stephen Boyd and Haya Harareet.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Jo Brand and Kerry Godliman head to Kent to search for antiques they can sell for a profit, accompanied by experts Catherine Southon and Steven Moore. Jo finds an enamel belt buckle at a budget price, but a three-figure sum spent on an object made from papier-mâché proves to be a gamble purchase. Meanwhile, Kerry has her eye on a Georgian fire-screen, and a piece of Chinese bronze.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Alex Brooker, Rhys Darby, Joanna Page and Molly Rainford test their general knowledge skills one last time before the winner is announced.(New).

programme.title: Celebrity Mastermind
programme.desc: Former Coronation Street star Colson Smith, radio presenter Nadia Jae, comedian Grace Campbell and magician Joel M are put to the test by Clive Myrie in the classic quiz where celebrities go under the spotlight.(New).

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts as the Cinephiles take on the Harlequins, with two British quizzers and their US captain taking on a British skipper and his two US team-mates. They must use patience, lateral thinking and sheer inspiration to make connections between four things that may appear at first not to be linked, with one set of clues asking what comes next in the sequence Reuben, Elvis, PB&J.

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.desc: It is the grand final of the 2025 Christmas competition, and Amol Rajan asks the questions, but it remains to be seen which team emerges victorious.(New).

programme.title: Operation Mincemeat
programme.desc: During the Second World War, two intelligence officers use a corpse and false papers to outwit German troops. Director John Madden's drama, starring Colin Firth, Matthew Macfadyen and Kelly Macdonald.

programme.title: The Damned Don't Cry
programme.desc: Living in Morocco, a mother and her teenage son travel to Tangier in search of new beginnings. Drama, with Abdellah El Hajjouji, Antoine Reinartz and Aicha Tebbae. In Arabic.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Officers raid a suburban house in Stornoway that they suspect is connected to drug dealing, while a man with a knife has barricaded himself in his Inverness home and police need to calm the situation before it gets out of control. In Ardnamurchan, police intervene as tensions mount between a protester and a fish farm.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Tensions are high as Agnes and the gang prepare for an incoming storm. Buster's flying high as he nervously awaits his birthday parachute jump, Winnie receives a shock to the system, and a lost nun is in need of help. Seasonal comedy capers, starring Brendan O'Carroll.

programme.title: Titanic Sinks Tonight

This opening instalment begins with lookout crew member Fred Fleet spotting a black mass right ahead of Titanic and alerting the navigation crew, but the ship still hits the iceberg and news of the damage filters through to the captain.

programme.title: Titanic Sinks Tonight
programme.desc: The captain orders the ship to be evacuated and tells the wireless operators to send out an urgent distress call to other ships, while down below in the boiler rooms, the crew pump out the incoming sea water to buy the ship more time. With only enough lifeboats for half the people on board, a rescue mission requires shuttle runs to be made to and from a rescue ship. First-class passengers are handed life-preservers and told to make their way to the boat deck, but they have not been told the ship is sinking.

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo start their own high-speed delivery service but need to know which top is best to go anbout their business.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: A meteor strikes Cosima and her dad's ship while they are exploring space and they crash-land on the planet of Proxima, where she makes a new best friend.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The heroes discover their latest quest - delivering 30 birthday balloons to Mr Friendlyface's cousin - isn't as easy as they expected.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: While falling, Grizzy performs a series of acrobatics that amazes the Lemmings.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Everyone ends up lost after losing their jar of Yummy in a labyrinth.

programme.title: Stage Stars
programme.desc: It is the start of a new year and the school is buzzing as borders find out who they are sharing a dorm with, and day pupils reunite at the lockers.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: A race around the ultimate obstacle course.

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and boxer Jackson take a time-out to make a fish finger sandwich that packs a punch.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Joel Mawhinney, Abby Cook and Shini Muthukrishnan learn about tigers and the Minecraft movie, Tigers and Henry the Dog.

programme.title: Lou
programme.desc: Pixar animation about a pile of lost and found items coming together to teach a toy-stealing schoolyard bully a valuable lesson.

programme.title: Deadly Mission Shark
programme.desc: Steve Backshall is on a mission to create a new generation of shark saviours, and takes 12 young UK hopefuls to boot camp with the challenge of choosing just six from the group.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: The giant armadillo, an animal so elusive few have ever seen it wild in the Brazilian wetlands region known as the Pantanal. David Attenborough reveals how the burrows the armadillos dig create homes for hundreds of other animals. Until recently man knew virtually nothing of this species, but Arnaud Desbiez, the founder of the Giant Armadillo Project, has changed all that.

programme.title: Carmen Jones
programme.desc: A sultry female military worker attracts admiring glances from her male colleagues, but she has her eye on an engaged pilot. Otto Preminger's romantic musical drama, based on Bizet's opera Carmen with modernised lyrics and set in the Deep South during the Second World War. Dorothy Dandridge, Harry Belafonte, Olga James and Pearl Bailey star.

programme.title: Mary Berry's Fantastic Feasts
programme.desc: Mary comes to the aid of three novice cooks - fireman Mark, youth worker Callum and boxing instructor Thaer, who want to throw a spectacular afternoon tea to say thank you to Soraya, who runs a youth charity in Cardiff. While the trio join Mary at her home for a series of cooking lessons, Roman Kemp and Tom Read Wilson oversee the extras to make the party extra special - and also offer moral support when temperatures rise in the kitchen. When everything is ready, they head to Langley Hall near Cardiff to cook their feast for 15, and give Soraya the surprise of a lifetime.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: The food writer uses a range of everyday spices to rustle up Thai spiced aubergines, chilli feta and a quick recipe for korma, before visiting two allotment-holders in Liverpool and preparing a tasty dish with their fresh produce.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Raymond and a team of volunteers give the valais blacknose sheep a bath, Kirsty and Tom rescue fallen sheep on the isle, and Stevie attempts to milk his first buffalo. In Shetland, Kirsty and Tom again row out to St Ninian's Isle to attempt to rescue a ewe and a lamb that have fallen from the isle's steep cliffs.

programme.title: Earth
programme.desc: Chris Packham presents this four-and-a-half-billion-year history of the planet, with each episode taking viewers on a journey through a pivotal moment when the Earth's future hung in the balance. The story begins with one of the darkest periods in the planet's history 252 million years ago - the worst mass extinction it has ever seen, when as much as 90 per cent of all species died.

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: A Nazi secret agent plans to kidnap Winston Churchill while the prime minister spends a weekend in the Norfolk countryside, and plants covert operatives in the area ready for his arrival. Second World War adventure, adapted from Jack Higgins' novel, starring Michael Caine, Donald Sutherland, Robert Duvall, Jenny Agutter, Donald Pleasence, Anthony Quayle and Jean Marsh.

programme.title: The Guns of Navarone
programme.desc: An elite group of Allied soldiers is dispatched to sabotage vital German artillery emplacements, despite the seemingly insurmountable odds and the suspicion there is a traitor in their midst. Oscar-winning Second World War adventure, based on Alistair MacLean's novel, starring Gregory Peck, David Niven, Anthony Quinn, Stanley Baker, Anthony Quayle and Irene Papas.

programme.title: Planet Earth III
programme.sub-title: Planet Earth III: Wonders of Nature
programme.desc: A compilation of highlights from the recent natural history documentary. In the Namib Desert, a pair of ostriches raise their family in the searing heat to keep them safe from predators - but time is ticking as the chicks begin to hatch. In the cold waters of North America, a little horn shark stumbles into an ambush set by an angel shark - but the potential victim has a secret weapon. In Botswana, newly hatched 'lily-trotter' chicks learn how to walk on water, and in Bali, long-tailed macaques steal tourists' valuable items - which they use to barter with staff for food.

programme.title: 40 Duets at the BBC
programme.desc: A selection from the BBC's music archives showcasing those hits that saw artists and acts joining forces to bring something new and unique to the UK charts. These are some of the biggest and best collaborations that remain classics to this day, featuring George Michael and Aretha Franklin, Eminem and Dido, Nelly and Kelly Rowland, Peter Gabriel and Kate Bush, Meat Loaf and Cher, Kenny Rogers and Dolly Parton, and Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan.(New).

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools looks back at performances on the show by unique combinations of artists, including Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash, Pops Staples and Carleen Anderson in 1994. There is a Dusty Springfield appearance in 1995 featuring Sinead O'Connor and Alison Moyet on backing vocals, as well as the memorable pairing of Nick Cave and Shane MacGowan from the show's first series in 1992. There are also more recent examples, with Damon Albarn and Kano teaming up in 2007 and Michael Kiwanuka and Little Simz in 2019.

programme.title: A Million Little Pieces
programme.desc: A drug-dependent man faces his past and his inner demons after he is interned in an institution for the addicted. Despite the rules of the centre that prevent all contact between men and women, who are treated in different pavilions, James meets Lilly, a beautiful and fragile young girl with a serious problem of addiction and emotional dependence. Drama, directed by Sam Taylor-Johnson and starring her husband Aaron Taylor-Johnson, alongside Billy Bob Thornton and Juliette Lewis.

programme.title: The Night Manager
programme.desc: Tom Hiddleston reprises his role as soldier-turned-hotel night manager Jonathan Pine in the long-awaited return of the acclaimed drama. The story picks up after nine years with Jonathan living as Alex Goodwin, a low-level MI6 officer running a quiet surveillance unit in London. His life is comfortingly uneventful until the chance sighting of former mercenary connected with arms dealer Richard Roper prompts a call to action and leads him to a violent encounter with a new player - Colombian businessman Teddy Dos Santos. Once in Colombia, Pine is plunged deep into a deadly plot to destabilise the country. With Olivia Colman, Diego Calva and Douglas Hodge.

programme.title: BBC Proms 2025
programme.desc: Claudia Winkleman hosts this musical exploration of her phenomenon ratings success. From epic classical orchestral favourites to opera excerpts with betrayal at their heart, this Prom, recorded in July at the Royal Albert Hall, features melodramatic chart tracks heard on the series with a gothic, symphonic twist. There's a new take on the theme tune and some familiar figures and faces from the challenges and round tables. Conjuring the misty intrigue are soloists Andrea Lykke, HAYLA and Darrell Smith, alongside the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra under conductor Karen Ní Bhroin and BBC Singers in works by composers including Rob Dougan, Sam Watts, Saint-Saëns, Mozart, Tchaikovsky and Puccini.

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Alex Brooker, Rhys Darby, Joanna Page and Molly Rainford test their general knowledge skills one last time before the winner is announced.

programme.title: Take a Hike
programme.desc: Competition held in a different part of Britain each week in which five people showcase countryside walks, with each judged by the other hikers on the quality of the route, the picnic, the views and the entertainment. Kicking off the first week in Devon is 63-year-old taxi driver Helen, who taking the others for a cultural tour of Ilfracombe's coastal path with a surprise splashy ending.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to the Cromarty Lighthouse Field Station at the edge of the Moray Firth, where scientists are tracking Scotland's resident bottlenose dolphins in the UK's longest-running study of its kind. As our seas face change, the findings are helping to build a picture of the wider health of our marine ecosystems. Plus, a look back through the archives, shining a light on conservation projects around the UK.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: A round-up of national and international news, plus current affairs, arts and entertainment, and weather.

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian Hamilton and his guide dog Major visit Alloa, which sits on the River Forth and was famous for brewing and glassmaking. He takes on a judo champion, visits a successful business on the high street, and hears about some dramatic paranormal events in the area. He and the crew also get the opportunity to try some handmade tablet, and Ian grabs the chance to take part in a tasting at Alloa's last brewery.(New).

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian Hamilton and his guide dog Major visit Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, which was built on fishing but reinvented itself with the arrival of oil and gas and is now looking towards renewables. Ian visits the fishmarket, plays crazy golf in a newly renovated town centre park and heads to the harbour to find out about a big new investment in the town.(New).

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt presents more highlights, with recipes by Asma Khan, Jane Baxter, Fernando Stovell and Shuana Froydenlund, while Rob Brydon faces his food heaven or hell.

programme.title: Mary Berry - Love to Cook
programme.desc: The culinary expert offers tips for cooking delicious meals, including aubergine caponata, a warming vegetable noodle soup, and her chicken and herb casserole. Mary Berry also meets fellow foodies who love growing their own ingredients.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Raymond's bull Major returns to work after being injured earlier in the year, but getting him to the field of cows involves a soggy detour. Raymond also travels to Switzerland with fiancee Jen to help their friends gather their valais blacknose sheep from the mountaintops. Kirsty and Aimee go sheep shopping to double their flock, while bad news forces buffalo farmer Stevie to make a shocking decision.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Bill Bailey narrates this natural history documentary telling the story of some of nature's most extraordinary partnerships, revealing what sometimes happens when animals need an itch scratching, help getting into food or home security assistance. The answer is, to find a partner - and not necessarily one of the same species. Highlights include hippos joining forces with fish for a full-body exfoliation and ravens inviting wolverines over for some bone-crunching assistance with their dinner.

programme.title: Chariots of Fire
programme.desc: Oscar-winning drama based on the true story of British runners Eric Liddell and Harold Abrahams, going for gold at the 1924 Olympics in Paris. The two athletes are driven by very different impulses - Liddell is inspired by his devout Christian faith, while Abrahams hopes to triumph over the anti-Semitism he has endured all his life. Starring Ian Charleson, Ben Cross, Nigel Havers, John Gielgud and Ian Holm. Vangelis provides the soundtrack.

programme.title: The Searchers
programme.desc: An embittered American Civil War veteran sets out to find his niece, who has been abducted by a renegade Comanche tribe. His search takes him many years, and during the long quest his travelling companion starts to wonder if he intends to rescue her or kill her. John Ford's Western, starring John Wayne, Natalie Wood, Jeffrey Hunter and Vera Miles.

programme.title: Ski Sunday
programme.desc: All the news, gossip and action from the piste.(New).

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are sent to Bolivia, where they are challenged to travel through the rainforest and journey to the coast of Chile, driving second-hand off-road vehicles bought locally for a maximum of £3,500 each. Along the way, they encounter drug lords and feel the effects of altitude sickness as they negotiate the region's roads, one of which is a notoriously dangerous 40-mile mountain pass dubbed El Camino de la Muerte - the Death Road.

programme.title: Pilgrimage with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Author and broadcaster Simon Reeve retraces the steps of British pilgrims, exploring the faith, hopes, desires and even the food that helped keep them on the road. In the first episode he sets out on a journey to Canterbury, beginning at the Holy Island of Lindisfarne off the coast of Northumberland, one of the earliest sites of Christian pilgrimage in Britain.

programme.title: The Million Pound Shaman Scam
programme.desc: Part one of two. Documentary about Hampstead fraudster Juliette D'Souza, who posed as a faith healer and conned her victims out of £1,000,000. In 2008, veteran journalist Tim Rayment received a tip about an incredibly bizarre crime in which an elite London community was ensnared in a dark web of spiritual manipulation, South American shamanism and millions of pounds in sacrificial offerings. At the centre of it all were a charming healer, a secretive woman and an invisible man named Papa Freddie.(New).

programme.title: Back to Black
programme.desc: The story of Amy Winehouse's life and career in music, following the development of her unique talent and passion. The film charts her teen years through to life in London's Camden Town, her tempestuous relationship with Blake Fielder-Civil and her development into a singular musician. Starring Marisa Abela, Jack O'Connell and Eddie Marsan.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools takes a look back at the singer's appearances on the music programme, having made her debut on the show in 2003 with her first single Stronger Than Me, taken from her debut album Frank. Amy returned to Later in 2006 after her number 1 Back to Black album to perform Top 10 hit Rehab and Motown-influenced Tears Dry on Their Own, as well as performing on the Hootenanny in 2004 and 2006, performing Teach Me Tonight, Monkey Man and teaming up with Paul Weller for a couple of numbers, including Etta Jones' Don't Go to Strangers.

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles and the team step in to help a youth club that has lost its home in the town of Beverley, East Yorkshire. The Cherry Tree Community Centre once gave local children a safe place to meet up and find support - but when the pandemic hit, the building was turned into a food hub for families, leaving the kids out in the cold. With another harsh winter on the way, Nick, designer Gabrielle Blackman and the DIY SOS regulars enlist the help of local tradespeople - as well as a few Gladiators - to construct a new, purpose-built youth centre on the edge of the park.

programme.title: The Traitors
programme.desc: Twenty-two people from across the UK descend on a Scottish castle in a bid to win up to £120,000, some to be assigned by host Claudia Winkleman as traitors, while the majority are faithful. Suspicions, secrets and lies echo around the castle, as under the cover of darkness, the Traitors must pick off the residual players one by one, eliminating them from the game. The faithful must try to work out who the traitors are in their midst, banishing them from the game before becoming their next victim. Those who make it to the final have a chance of winning the life-changing cash prize.

Fiona is also challenged by Will Farmer to work out the values of three examples of ceramic Lustreware, and delves into the history of the gardens themselves and their close association with the nearby potteries.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A further selection of creepy-crawly close-ups, focusing on courtship in the bug world. Highlights include scorpions shaking their booty, the perfume-wearing nasonia wasp and the tropical cricket, for whom romance goes out of the window as it uses bribery to seal the deal with would-be partners. One potential partner to steer well clear of, however, is the praying mantis, the female of which is notorious for eating the male just after - or even during - mating. Narrated by David Attenborough.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A close-up view of sex, bug-style, as David Attenborough talks viewers through the different ways in which creepy-crawlies reproduce. Size matters for the minuscule male orb spider, creepily sneaking up on its intended and trying to mate without her noticing, while there's no rest for the lothario-like butterfly, which has plenty of notches on its proverbial bedpost. However, the harvestman spider has no use for sex at all, and reproduces by cloning itself.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough shifts the focus to bugs that prefer co-operation rather than conflict. They include burrowing cockroaches, the suitably named social spiders - which share a 30-metre web - the queen bee and her happy hive of workers and green ants pulling together to build a nest.

programme.title: Shark with Steve Backshall

programme.title: Shark: British Isles Special with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall goes in search of some of the 30-plus shark species that inhabit waters of the British Isles, showing how the big fish in home waters are just as astonishing and mysterious as their global cousins. Along the way he encounters a four-ton basking shark near the Hebrides and dives with his favourite of all time, the blue shark, off the coast of Cornwall. He also meets scientists and conservationists in Wales who are working to protect endangered species.

programme.title: Big Cats: An Amazing Animal Family
programme.desc: Part one of two. Biologist Patrick Aryee explores how cats have evolved throughout the millennia, learning to thrive in inhospitable environments, as well as becoming the world's most popular pet. In the first edition there is spectacular footage of caracals jumping three metres to catch flying birds, and a rare Bornean bay cat, which was thought to have been extinct. Patrick finds out how tigers made the transition from South-east Asia's steamy jungles to the -40C temperatures of Siberia, and meets 'lion whisperer' Kevin Richardson.

programme.title: Big Cats: An Amazing Animal Family
programme.desc: Patrick Aryee concludes his two-part exploration of the feline family tree, revealing how the Canadian lynx learned to thrive in the snow and spread out, evolving and inhabiting new parts of the Americas. In Belize, he mounts an experiment that showcases the margay's supersharp senses and gravity-defying acrobatics, and heads to the training track with a cheetah to find out what speed it is capable of. Finally, Patrick tells the story of the cat's domestication in Essaouira, Morocco, believed to be one of the first places where one particular species first gave up life in the wild in return for food, warmth, security and a home.

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the first of a two-part documentary, the naturalist explores the origins of life on Earth. Beginning the journey near his childhood home in Charnwood Forest, Leicestershire, he learns how a fossil discovery transformed scientists' understanding of the evolution of complex organisms, and in Newfoundland and Australia he reveals the earliest kinds of animal to exist on the planet. With the help of cutting-edge technology and visual effects, the programme brings the creatures to life, demonstrating how they survived.

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the conclusion of the two-part documentary, the naturalist travels to Burgess Shale in Canada's Rocky Mountains, where he explores how evolution gained pace once creatures developed mouths and mobility. In Scotland, he reveals that one of the smallest fossils found holds the secret to how animals began surviving on dry land, and explains the bloom of life during the oxygen-rich Carboniferous period.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster concludes his close-up examination of the creepy-crawly world, shifting focus to the bugs' ultimate invention - the colony. Key residents of these minuscule mega-cities include honey bees, termites, leafcutter ants - who have a knack for farming - and their Argentine cousins, members of a community so vast it spans an entire continent.

programme.title: Attenborough's Journey
programme.desc: Documentary following David Attenborough as he journeys around the world to make his series First Life, which explores the origins of life on Earth. As he visits locations including the Great Barrier Reef, the deserts of Morocco and the glaciers of Canada, the broadcaster and wildlife expert explains his life-long fascination with the natural world, and also travels back to Leicestershire, the county in which he spent his childhood.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: The naturalist and film-maker explores the many varieties of plant life housed at the Royal Botanic Gardens in Kew, west London, and explains what they reveal about the natural world and the development of life on Earth. He begins inside the establishment's Palm House, whose climate has been engineered to simulate conditions found in rainforests, charting the evolution of plants that grow in the world's wettest regions and investigating how flowering plants spread across the globe so rapidly.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: The naturalist explores how the plants at Kew Gardens change through the seasons and demonstrates the surprising properties of several species, including the predatory pond-dwelling bladderwort utricularia and a fungus that appears to be capable of mind control. He also discusses the largest single organism on the planet, visits the world's biggest flower and explains how plants and insects can communicate using scents and music.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: The naturalist concludes his exploration of the Royal Botanic Gardens in Kew, west London, by examining plants that have evolved to minimise their dependence on water, enabling them to survive in the world's driest environments. He witnesses a cactus blooming at midnight, tells the story of the spectacular flowering of the Agave franzosinii, and visits the Millennium Seed Bank, a facility designed to save plants from future extinction.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough

This first episode examines the survival tactics of its terrifying residents including killer ants, trap-setting spiders and beetles with the ability to shoot boiling chemicals at their enemies.

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster continues his bug-eyed view of the world of creepy-crawlies, revealing how predators defuse the defences of their prey. Highlights include the cockroach wasp, busy preparing a tasty - and very live - treat for its young, the whirligig beetle, which employs a water-based radar system, and the jumping portia spider, which feeds on other arachnids.

He uses fossils of both ancient and living species combined with CGI and film to chart their journey out of the water to populate all corners of the globe.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals
